toolchains.note: The host C compiler CMake already uses. C99 is the floor: the public headers use nothing newer, and the gate is what keeps it that way.
The host C++ compiler. A C ABI that a C++ consumer cannot include is only half an ABI, so every header is compiled in both languages.
GCC by name, including C23, which the host compiler may predate.
GCC's C++ driver at the standards CNA itself builds with.
A second front end catches what one compiler's extensions would hide.
Clang's C++ driver, for the same reason.
A Windows target reached by cross-compiling. Headers only: nothing here links or runs a Windows binary, and the matrix says so rather than implying a tested platform.

configurations.note: No window, no GPU. Every route that needs neither is proven here, and every route that does is proven to refuse.
SDL's own 2D renderer under the dummy video driver, with the CNA_DEVICES half of devices-ext compiled in.
A CPU rasteriser: a third backend answer for every capability query, and the compiled-out devices half again.

AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer with leak detection on. This is what catches a handle that outlives its owner or an operation nobody released. It runs the CPU rasteriser with the devices half compiled in, which is the one pairing the other three rows leave out: SOFTWARE is therefore exercised in both CNA_DEVICES states.

unsupported.subject: Running a Windows binary
unsupported.note: The cross-compiler proves the headers parse for a Windows target; nothing here links or executes one, so no Windows behaviour is claimed.

unsupported.subject: macOS, iOS, Android and the web targets
unsupported.note: No toolchain for any of them is present, so no cell exists for them at all rather than an untested claim.

unsupported.subject: C89
unsupported.note: The headers use `//` comments and mixed declarations, so C99 is the floor by design rather than by accident.

unsupported.subject: Renderers other than the four configured
unsupported.note: CNA has 49 renderer identities; four are built and run here. The other 45 share the same C surface, and the capability queries are what a caller uses to find out what any of them supports.
